Ash Patel: Heads up — premerge SAST flagged `Potential Hardcoded Key` inside `vendor/gen/thirdparty/auth.go`. Looks like generated code, probably a false positive. Anyone owns the rule provenance?
Sara Nguyen: can you paste the finding + file snippet? :eyes:
Ash Patel: pasted below. this came from yesterday's nightly run.
Ash Patel: ```diff
--- a/vendor/gen/thirdparty/auth.go
+++ b/vendor/gen/thirdparty/auth.go
@@
-    var key = "AKIA..."
+    var key = "REDACTED_GENERATED_TOKEN"
```
Ash Patel: scanner shows full literal in CI report, but locally the file has `REDACTED_GENERATED_TOKEN`. suspect the scanner fetched submodule or generated artifact that still had placeholder replaced by a build-time token.
dev-tools-bot: scanbot queued run #17902 — SAST found 1 high, 3 medium. metadata: rule=hardcoded-key, fingerprint=sha256:8f9c, collector=gha-scan.
Mike O'Connor: hmm — does the repo use a git submodule or a fetch step that pulls a private artifact? That could be where the token was injected.
Ash Patel: yes — we pull a private proto repo as a submodule in CI via a deploy-bot token stored in Vault. The scanner runs inside the same runner and the checkout step uses that token to fetch. I think the token got written into generated code during `protoc` step.
Julian: If that's the case, we should not change scanner RBAC broadly. We can either: 1) make scanner fetch an unpopulated artifact (no secrets), 2) add a suppression for generated paths with evidence, or 3) change the generator to never emit literals.
Priya Raman: For (2) we need audit trail. Security policy requires a suppression PR with evidence + two approvers (sec + owner) and a timestamped decision. Also we need to ensure KMS/Vault decrypt events are logged for that run.
Sara Nguyen: who can confirm whether KMS decrypts are already in our central audit logs for that runner? @Mike?
Mike O'Connor: KMS CloudAudit logs are on. But decrypt events from ephemeral runner tokens may be routed via the ephemeral service account. We currently log the KMS key usage, but we don't always correlate runner instance id -> CI run id. We should add the CI run id as an attribute in the decrypt call so logs are searchable.
Ash Patel: actionable plan suggestion: (A) create a suppression entry scoped to `vendor/gen/**` with a one-week expiration, (B) open a follow-up to remove token emission at source, (C) add CI attribute `ci.run_id` to KMS decrypts and S3 fetch calls.
Julian: +1 to that. For suppression evidence, please attach: the exact file diff, full scanner raw output, and a small script showing repro. The suppression entry should reference the fingerprint `sha256:8f9c`.
Priya Raman: Also require that any suppression PR updates the suppression index and triggers a security review checklist. If suppression is >7 days, escalate to policy board.
scanbot: suppression request template: `/suppress rule=hardcoded-key scope=vendor/gen/** fingerprint=sha256:8f9c expires=2025-05-27 reason="generated artifact; token injected by CI checkout" evidence=link-to-artifact`
Ash Patel: created PR draft: https://github.com/redwood/example/pull/423 — includes diff, raw scan output, and `repro.sh` that demonstrates token emission when running protoc with deploy-bot token.
Sara Nguyen: I'll review evidence today. Quick Q: do we want to change runner permissions instead of suppression? i.e., run scanner in a checkout step before fetching private submodule.
Mike O'Connor: that might be simpler: reorder steps so scanner runs before `git submodule update --init --recursive` that requires the deploy token. But some builds need the generated protos for build-time linting. If we do that we must preserve dev UX.
Priya Raman: whichever route chosen, add an audit requirement: all KMS decrypts must include `ci.run_id` and `repo` tags, kept for 90 days in the audit log retention. Security will run a one-off query to confirm the suppression run.
Julian: small note — if we modify CI to reorder, we should add a canary: run both workflows for 3 days and compare results. Avoid blind removal of protections.
Ash Patel: timeline: I will (1) update CI to add `ci.run_id` metadata to decrypts (PR in infra repo), (2) open suppression PR for `vendor/gen/**` (draft already), (3) schedule generator fix ticket to remove token emission. Target: suppression + audit metadata by EOD tomorrow, generator fix in next sprint.
Sara Nguyen: ack. I'll be reviewer on suppression PR. Priya will sign off for security. Mike — can you make the CI metadata change a high-priority patch?
Mike O'Connor: will do. I'll open infra PR and tag `@dev-tools` and `@security` in review.
Priya Raman: Thanks — once suppression is merged, I'll run an evidence query and mark the finding as suppressed in tracker. Reminder: if suppression turns out to be risky, security can revoke quickly.
Ash Patel: Thanks all. Filing a short incident-note link in the PR per policy (in case this crops up again).
Sara Nguyen: +1 — thanks.
Julian: leaving a TODO: add a test that fails if any generated file contains patterns matching `AKIA|REDACTED` before publishing artifacts.
Ash Patel: noted. I'll add the test to the generator repo.
dev-tools-bot: action items recorded: infra/PR# (add KMS metadata), example/PR#423 (suppression draft), generator/issue#989.
Priya Raman: closing loop tomorrow after I run the audit query. :white_check_mark:
